candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 1:50. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13 (Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On the setting-apart of the Levites for tabernacle service, Ephrem reads the census-and-separation pattern of Num 1:50 as the canonical model for ordered ministry: the people are numbered for their tribes, but one tribe is numbered for the Lord himself. The Levites' exemption from the military census is not privilege but conscription into a more dangerous service — the daily handling of the holy things. Tewahedo monastic theology cites Num 1:50 as the Old-Testament warrant for the consecration of the däbtära and the priest-monks; the consecrated are numbered for the sanctuary first, for the nation only afterward.
